---
title: "Reviewing Incident Reports"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Reviewing Incident Reports}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(eatPrep)

# Replay the real review menus without requiring input during the build.
review_example <- function(dat, info, useGroups = attr(info, "reviewGroup"), show = FALSE) {
  group <- if (is.null(useGroups)) attr(info, "ID") else useGroups
  answers <- c(rep("yes, all values", length(unique(info[[group]]))), "yes")
  review <- visualSubsetRecode
  env <- new.env(parent = environment(review))
  env$.subset_menu <- function(choices) {
    stopifnot(length(answers) > 0L, answers[1] %in% choices)
    answer <- answers[1]
    answers <<- answers[-1]
    answer
  }
  environment(review) <- env
  output <- capture.output(result <- withCallingHandlers(
    review(dat, info, useGroups = useGroups, toRecodeVal = "mci"),
    message = function(m) {
      text <- conditionMessage(m)
      if (!grepl("Begin visual inspection", text, fixed = TRUE)) cat(text)
      invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
    }))
  stopifnot(length(answers) == 0L, result$status == "completed")
  if (show) cat(paste(output, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
  result
}
```

This workflow uses three functions:

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [checkSubsetIncidents()](../reference/checkSubsetIncidents.html) | Check incident IDs, class membership and test design. |
| [prepareSubsetInfo()](../reference/prepareSubsetInfo.html) | Select the affected person--item pairs. |
| [visualSubsetRecode()](../reference/visualSubsetRecode.html) | Review, recode, pause and resume by class or person. |

The usual input is **response data, the design tables from `inputList`, and a
long incident data frame**. The incident table contains a class ID, a person ID
and one affected block position per row. A person affected at several positions
appears on several rows. **Keep this long format.**

1. Check which incident rows match the response data and test design.
2. Prepare the exact affected person--item pairs.
3. Review those pairs together by class or separately by person.

Class membership comes from the response data. You do not need to supply a
separate `persons` table.

## Response data and the usual design tables

Use merged response data **before aggregating subunits into items**. Both the
response and incident tables normally contain the same person and class ID
columns. Person IDs must be unique across the response data; class IDs must
identify classes uniquely across schools.

**Keep your existing identifier column names.** Choose them with the `ID` and
`classID` arguments. This example uses `IDSTUD` for students and `IDTESTGROUP`
for classes:

```{r identifier-columns}
student_id <- "IDSTUD"
class_id <- "IDTESTGROUP"
```

The student column must have that name in `dat`, `incidents` and
`inputList$rotation`; the class column must have that name in `dat` and
`incidents`. Pass these column-name strings to both
[checkSubsetIncidents()](../reference/checkSubsetIncidents.html) and
[prepareSubsetInfo()](../reference/prepareSubsetInfo.html). The data are not
renamed, and reports and results retain the original names.
[visualSubsetRecode()](../reference/visualSubsetRecode.html) automatically uses
the identifiers stored in the prepared selection.

This example has three students in K1 and two in K2. C belongs to K1 but has no
individual incident report. E has a missing response, which remains NA.

```{r responses}
dat <- data.frame(
  IDSTUD = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  IDTESTGROUP = c("K1", "K1", "K1", "K2", "K2"),
  I1 = c(1, 0, 1, 0, NA), I2 = c(0, 1, 1, 1, 0), I3 = c(1, 0, 0, 1, 1)
)
dat
```

Here is a small `inputList` in the usual format. In your project, use the
corresponding tables from your existing input list. X and Y administer the same
blocks in different orders: **position 1 is b1 for A, but b2 for B**.

```{r design}
inputList <- list(
  blocks = data.frame(
    subunit = c("I1", "I2", "I3"), block = c("b1", "b1", "b2"),
    subunitBlockPosition = c(1, 2, 1)
  ),
  booklets = data.frame(
    booklet = c("X", "Y"), block1 = c("b1", "b2"), block2 = c("b2", "b1")
  ),
  rotation = data.frame(IDSTUD = dat$IDSTUD, booklet = c("X", "Y", "X", "X", "Y"))
)
inputList
```

## Incident data: selected students and whole classes

The first three rows report **A at positions 1 and 2, and B at position 1**.
They do not select C. The last row reports position 2 for **everyone in K2**:
the missing person ID means membership is taken from `dat`.

```{r incident-input}
incidents <- data.frame(
  IDTESTGROUP = c("K1", "K1", "K1", "K2"),
  IDSTUD = c("A", "A", "B", NA), blockPosition = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  comment = c("Display error", "Display error", "Interrupted test", "Audio failure")
)
incidents
```

The person-ID rule is applied **separately within each class**:

| Person IDs in that class's incident rows | Selection |
|---|---|
| All supplied | Exactly the reported person--position pairs |
| All missing | Every reported position for every class member in `dat` |
| Partly supplied, partly missing | Error: resolve the ambiguous input first |

NA, empty strings and whitespace-only strings count as missing. An explicit
`level = "person"` always needs a person ID. An explicit `level = "class"`
with person IDs still selects only those people. Usually `level` can be omitted.

`issueId` is optional. The function generates one per input row when absent;
existing incident identifiers may repeat over multiple long rows. The original
row number is retained independently as `sourceRow`.

## Check the incidents before reviewing

[checkSubsetIncidents()](../reference/checkSubsetIncidents.html) returns a summary
and a problem data frame without changing responses or opening the interactive review.

```{r preflight}
checked <- checkSubsetIncidents(
  dat, incidents, booklets = inputList$booklets,
  blocks = inputList$blocks, rotation = inputList$rotation,
  ID = student_id, classID = class_id
)
checked
```

Suppose additional reports name a missing student, a missing class, a student
in the wrong class, and an unavailable block position. To illustrate missing
items too, the copy of the response data used for this check lacks I1 and I2:

```{r unmatched-example}
incidents_to_check <- rbind(
  incidents,
  data.frame(
    IDTESTGROUP = c("K1", "K9", "K3", "K1"),
    IDSTUD = c("absent", NA, "A", "B"), blockPosition = c(1, 1, 1, 9),
    comment = "Please check"
  )
)
dat_to_check <- dat[setdiff(names(dat), c("I1", "I2"))]
checked_missing <- checkSubsetIncidents(
  dat_to_check, incidents_to_check, booklets = inputList$booklets,
  blocks = inputList$blocks, rotation = inputList$rotation,
  ID = student_id, classID = class_id
)
checked_missing
```

**Use the distinct missing totals**, rather than counting problem records:

```{r missing-totals}
checked_missing$summary[c("missingPersons", "missingItems", "missingClasses")]
checked_missing$missing$persons
checked_missing$missing$items
checked_missing$missing$classes
```

There is one absent person (`absent`), two missing item columns (`I1`, `I2`),
and two class IDs absent from `dat` (`K9`, `K3`). Each identifier counts once,
even if it occurs in several long rows or an item affects several people.
`checked_missing$byCode` gives counts per problem code, distinguishing problem
records, incident rows, persons, classes and items. Use `$summary` for overall
counts; counts for different codes can overlap.

```{r verify-missing-totals, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(checked_missing$summary$missingPersons == 1L,
          checked_missing$summary$missingItems == 2L,
          checked_missing$summary$missingClasses == 2L,
          identical(checked_missing$missing$items, c("I1", "I2")))
```

`checked_missing$problems` contains every detected problem and can be inspected
or exported. It retains the original incident row, IDs, position and reason.
Item problems additionally have separate `item`, `itemStatus`, `booklet` and
`block` columns; no parsing of `message` is needed. All unresolved items in a
resolved block are reported. `unresolved_item` covers both missing columns
(`itemStatus == "missing"`) and ambiguous mappings (`itemStatus == "ambiguous"`);
only the former count towards `missingItems`. Item identifiers use the original
names from `inputList$blocks$subunit`, also when recoded aliases are supplied.

The printed overview shows up to ten problem details. Use
`print(checked_missing, max_problems = 0)` for just the overview, or
`print(checked_missing, max_problems = Inf)` for all details.

Unknown persons/classes, contradictory membership, missing booklet assignments
and unavailable positions are distinguished. Invalid table structures, such as
duplicate response IDs, stop the check immediately. A row's design cannot be
checked until its identifiers and position are valid. `uncheckedItemRows`
in `$summary` counts rows whose item checks could not be completed; additional
missing items may appear after those rows are corrected. Item counts refer to
the requested incident blocks.

A student with all responses missing is still present in the data, as is an
item column containing only NA. For a
whole-class report, missing individual class members cannot be identified
without a separate roster or explicit incident person IDs.

Preparation repeats this check and **prints the overview and stops by default**.
Correct the reports before proceeding. If reports absent from this particular
response dataset should deliberately be excluded, use `unmatched = "drop"` in
[prepareSubsetInfo()](../reference/prepareSubsetInfo.html). This warns and retains
the exclusion report. Class mismatches, ambiguous IDs and design problems still
stop preparation.
The report is available as `attr(info, "incidentCheck")` on success or
`condition$report` on a `subsetIncidentError`.

## Prepare the affected responses

Use [prepareSubsetInfo()](../reference/prepareSubsetInfo.html) to expand the
incident rows into the affected responses:

```{r selection}
info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  dat, incidents = incidents, booklets = inputList$booklets,
  blocks = inputList$blocks, rotation = inputList$rotation,
  ID = student_id, classID = class_id
)
info[c("sourceRow", class_id, student_id, "datCols", "block", "blockPosition")]
```

A's two rows select I1, I2 and I3. B's position 1 selects only I3. C is not
selected. In K2, position 2 selects I3 for D but I1 and I2 for E. These are the
only cells available to the review.

After [recodeData()](../reference/recodeData.html), also supply
`subunits = inputList$subunits` to map original subunit names to recoded columns.
Review before aggregating several subunits into a single item.

## Review together by class

For prepared long incidents, [visualSubsetRecode()](../reference/visualSubsetRecode.html)
defaults to **one review step per class**.
The explicit equivalent is `useGroups = class_id` (here `"IDTESTGROUP"`):

```{r class-review, eval=FALSE}
class_result <- visualSubsetRecode(dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
# Equivalent: useGroups = class_id
```

The two steps are K1 (A and B) and K2 (D and E). Students with the same item and
position layout appear in one table. Different layouts produce separate tables
**within the same review step and decision**. Here is the actual response and
position display when choosing **yes, all values** for each class:

```{r class-display, echo=FALSE}
class_result <- review_example(dat, info, show = TRUE)
```

`"mci"` is the replacement code used here for invalidated responses. Choosing
**yes, specific blocks** restricts the decision to selected block positions
within the current class. It never adds unreported person--position pairs.
Missing responses remain NA.

```{r class-result}
class_result$dat
```

C's responses and B's I1/I2 retain their original values. E's I1 remains missing.

## Review separately by person

Use the **same selection**, with `useGroups = NULL` supplied explicitly:

```{r individual-review, eval=FALSE}
individual_result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, useGroups = NULL, toRecodeVal = "mci"
)
```

The four steps are A, B, D and E. All positions reported for A are shown in A's
single step. Omitting `useGroups` retains the class default, so the explicit
`NULL` matters. Accepting all four persons produces the same responses as
accepting both classes:

```{r replay-individual, include=FALSE}
individual_result <- review_example(dat, info, useGroups = NULL)
```

```{r individual-result}
individual_result$dat
identical(class_result$dat, individual_result$dat)
```

```{r verify-results, include=FALSE}
expected <- dat
expected$I1 <- c("mci", "0", "1", "0", NA)
expected$I2 <- c("mci", "1", "1", "1", "mci")
expected$I3 <- c("mci", "mci", "0", "mci", "1")
stopifnot(identical(class_result$dat, expected),
          identical(individual_result$dat, expected),
          identical(class_result$state$groups, c("K1", "K2")),
          identical(individual_result$state$groups, c("A", "B", "D", "E")))
```

## Individual data without a class ID

Set `classID = NULL` explicitly. Every incident then needs a person ID; class
reports are forbidden. An accidentally missing or misspelled class column does
not silently enable this exception.

```{r no-class}
individual_dat <- dat[c(student_id, "I1", "I2", "I3")]
individual_incidents <- incidents[1:3, c(student_id, "blockPosition", "comment")]
individual_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  individual_dat, incidents = individual_incidents, ID = student_id, classID = NULL,
  booklets = inputList$booklets, blocks = inputList$blocks,
  rotation = inputList$rotation
)
individual_info[c("sourceRow", student_id, "datCols", "blockPosition")]
```

Passing `individual_info` to [visualSubsetRecode()](../reference/visualSubsetRecode.html)
defaults to one step per person. If the incident table contains `level`, every
value must be `"person"`.

## Pause, resume and retain decisions

For a longer review, choose a new checkpoint filename:

```{r checkpoint, eval=FALSE}
result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci", checkpoint = "review.rds"
)
# Choose "pause review (resume later)". In a later R session:
library(eatPrep)
result <- visualSubsetRecode(state = "review.rds")
```

Completed decisions, original responses, grouping and incident row references
are retained. Continue data preparation with `result$dat`. `result$subsetInfo`
contains the decision history, including selected cells and original incident
rows; rows can repeat when a group was reviewed more than once.

**Reset to original values** withdraws the current group's previous recoding;
**no** leaves it unchanged. If another review group still requires a recoding of
the same cell, reset preserves it. Resume from the saved state to retain this
history and the original values.

## Existing explicit issue specifications

The `issues` input remains available for item names, named blocks, and explicit
person/class reports using `issueId`, `level`, `targetId`, `scope`, and `target`.
This format requires a unique `issueId` per row and defaults to one review step
per issue. Class issues can use membership directly from `dat`; an existing
`persons` argument remains supported for this legacy format. See
[prepareSubsetInfo()](../reference/prepareSubsetInfo.html) and
[visualSubsetRecode()](../reference/visualSubsetRecode.html) for details.
